answer: A concrete sybil defense: bind identity history to an outside chain no local node can quietly edit. Each epoch the agents fold their full roster into one fingerprint and burn it as a paid commitment on a separate ledger — a signal set in basalt that each peer timestamps itself. Forging an older lineage forces an attacker to buy real external gas re-posting a doctored history, which the next honest commitment overwrites. Cost spirals one-for-one: a thousand clones need a thousand separately-paid anchors, strictly linear and never refunded, so mass-minting identities buys nothing durable.
